# {{title}}

> {{title}} runs on Mavi CMS. Its posts, categories, tags, uploaded files and
> forms all live behind one HTTP API, and this file is what a program — or
> somebody's assistant — needs in order to build pages out of them.

This file is served by the site it describes, so every address in it is this
site's and no other's. One server answers for many sites and the host name is
the whole of the difference between them: copy the addresses exactly as they
are written here rather than assembling them from a hostname you were told
somewhere else.

- API: {{base}}
- Panel: {{origin}}/admin
- Interactive docs: {{origin}}/scalar
- OpenAPI: {{base}}/api-docs/openapi.json

## Getting in

Reading needs an account on this site. A build is not a person and has none:
it is handed a build token, made in the panel under **API**, which can read
this site, can change nothing, and lasts thirty days. Put it in the
environment as `CMS_TOKEN` and send it as a bearer token.

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CMS_TOKEN" \
  '{{base}}/posts?status=published&include=content&limit=100'
```

Somebody working in a browser signs in at the panel and gets a cookie instead.
The two are the same session by different routes; a token is the one to use
anywhere a person is not sitting.

A token that writes does not exist. If something you are building has to
create or change a post it signs in as an account with a password, and that is
a different and larger decision than reading.

Three addresses answer to anybody at all, because the visitor filling in a
contact form or a newsletter box has no account here:
`GET /forms/{slug}/schema`, `POST /forms/{slug}/submit` and
`POST /mail/subscribe`.

## If you are an assistant

There is a shorter way in than this document. The same address answers the
Model Context Protocol at `{{base}}/mcp`, where the site is a set of tools
rather than an API to read about: finding and reading posts, writing and
correcting them, what has come in through the forms, and building the pages.
The tools you are offered depend on the token you send — a build token is
offered only the ones that read.

```
claude mcp add --transport http mavicms {{base}}/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $CMS_TOKEN"
```

Somewhere that has no field for a token — Claude's own connector dialog,
ChatGPT's — paste the address on its own. This site is its own authorization
server: you will be sent here to sign in and asked whether to allow it, and
the program is handed a credential you never see. It is listed under **API**
in the panel afterwards and can be disconnected there.

Nothing there deletes anything.

The rest of this file is for building a front end, which is a different job:
a build reads the API directly, at the addresses below.

## Reading

| Method | Address | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/posts` | Posts, newest first, in pages. |
| GET | `/posts/{id}` | One post, with its sibling languages. |
| GET | `/categories` | Categories, per language. |
| GET | `/tags` | Tags, per language. |
| GET | `/languages` | The languages this site writes in. |
| GET | `/media` | Uploaded files and their addresses. |
| GET | `/forms` | The forms this site accepts answers on. |

`GET /posts` takes:

- `status` — comma-separated. **A build wants `status=published`.** Left out,
  every status comes back and drafts go online.
- `locale` — comma-separated language codes. Left out, every language comes
  back, which is what a site with one language wants and never what a site
  with three does.
- `include=content` — adds `content_html` and `content_markdown` to each item.
  A listing leaves the bodies out otherwise, because a whole archive in one
  response is megabytes nobody asked for.
- `include=seo` — adds `seo_title`, `seo_description` and `canonical`, which
  are what a page's `<head>` is made of. Without it a listing has no SEO
  fields at all and reading them gives nothing back rather than an error, so a
  site can ship with the CMS's titles silently unused. Ask for both at once
  with `include=content,seo`.
- `limit` (default 50, maximum 200) and `offset`.
- `q` — free text across titles, summaries and bodies.
- `slug` — an exact address, for asking whether one post exists.

The answer is `{ items, total, limit, offset, counts }`. Page with `offset`
until you have `total`; do not assume one request is the archive.

### What a post looks like

```json
{
  "id": "0198c0de-0000-7000-8000-000000000000",
  "title": "A title",
  "slug": "a-title",
  "excerpt": "One paragraph, for cards and meta description fallbacks.",
  "status": "published",
  "publish_at": null,
  "author": "Somebody",
  "category": "Notes",
  "category_ids": ["0198c0de-0000-7000-8000-000000000001"],
  "tags": ["one", "two"],
  "cover_url": "/uploads/2026/08/cover.png",
  "featured": false,
  "locale": "en",
  "translation_group_id": "0198c0de-0000-7000-8000-000000000002",
  "locales": ["en", "tr"],
  "digest": "6f1e0a2b4c8d9e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f6071",
  "created_at": "2026-08-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-02T11:30:00+00:00",
  "content_html": "<p>…</p>",
  "content_markdown": "…"
}
```

Worth knowing about the fields:

- **`digest`** is a fingerprint of everything the post renders to. It changes
  when the post changes and does not change when the row is merely saved
  again, so it is what a build should key its cache on. It is on every item of
  a listing whether or not the bodies were asked for, which is what makes it
  possible to find out what changed without downloading the archive.
- **`content_markdown`** is the canonical form and `content_html` is what it
  renders to. The Markdown is written for [comark](https://comark.dev), so a
  project that wants its own components for blocks parses the Markdown; a
  project that wants the post as it stands uses the HTML.
- **`locales`** lists every language this post exists in, and
  `translation_group_id` is shared by all of them. Together they are enough to
  emit `hreflang` alternates without a request per language.
- **`cover_url`** and any address inside the content that begins with `/` is
  on this server: put `{{origin}}` in front of it. When the site uploads to
  object storage the addresses are already absolute.
- **`status`** is `draft`, `review`, `scheduled` or `published`. A scheduled
  post has a `publish_at` and becomes published on its own within a minute of
  it, and the site is asked to build. So a build that asks for `published`
  gets the post the first time it runs after the time the writer picked, and
  nothing has to poll for it.

### Asking again, cheaply

`GET /posts` carries an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` and a listing
that has not changed answers `304` with no body at all. A development server
that reloads on every save, and a build that runs after a change to one post,
both spend nothing to learn that the other nine hundred posts are as they
were.

## Sending

Forms are made in the panel, so no fixed description can say which fields one
takes. Ask it, then send it:

```
curl {{base}}/forms/contact/schema
```

```json
{
  "name": "Contact",
  "slug": "contact",
  "fields": [
    { "name": "email", "label": "Email", "type": "email", "required": true },
    { "name": "message", "label": "Message", "type": "textarea", "required": true }
  ]
}
```

```
curl -X POST {{base}}/forms/contact/submit \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"someone@example.com","message":"Hello"}'
```

A key the form does not define is refused rather than quietly kept, so send
what the schema lists and nothing else. Neither address needs a token. A form
that has been switched off answers `404` rather than saying it exists.

A newsletter box is the same shape, against a list that has been made public
in the panel:

```
curl -X POST {{base}}/mail/subscribe \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"someone@example.com","name":"","lists":["news"]}'
```

It answers `202` whether or not anything was sent: on a double opt-in list
nothing goes out until the address answers a confirmation, and the page should
say so rather than say "you are subscribed".

## Astro

What follows is a whole working connection for Astro 7.2 or newer. It reads
this site at build time, rebuilds only the pages whose posts changed, and
needs nothing beyond `astro` itself.

### 1. The environment

```
CMS_API_URL={{base}}
CMS_TOKEN=…
```

`CMS_TOKEN` comes from **API → Build tokens** in the panel. It is shown once.
A build with no token sees nothing, and "why are there no posts" is almost
always this.

### 2. `src/loaders/mavicms.ts`

```ts
import type { Loader } from "astro/loaders"

// Astro reads .env into import.meta.env; CI usually sets the environment
// itself and leaves that empty, so take either.
const API = import.meta.env.CMS_API_URL ?? process.env.CMS_API_URL
const TOKEN = import.meta.env.CMS_TOKEN ?? process.env.CMS_TOKEN
const PAGE = 200

interface Summary {
  id: string
  slug: string
  digest: string
  locale: string
}

export function posts({ locale }: { locale?: string } = {}): Loader {
  return {
    name: "mavicms-posts",
    load: async ({ store, meta, logger, parseData }) => {
      if (!TOKEN) throw new Error("CMS_TOKEN is not set; the CMS will answer nothing")

      const get = async (path: string, init?: RequestInit) => {
        const response = await fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
          ...init,
          headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, ...init?.headers },
        })
        if (!response.ok && response.status !== 304) {
          throw new Error(`${path} answered ${response.status}`)
        }
        return response
      }

      // The index carries every post's digest and none of the bodies, so it is
      // small enough to ask for in full every time — and when it has not
      // changed the server sends nothing back at all.
      const index: Summary[] = []
      for (let offset = 0; ; offset += PAGE) {
        const query = new URLSearchParams({
          status: "published",
          limit: String(PAGE),
          offset: String(offset),
        })
        if (locale) query.set("locale", locale)

        // The tag is only worth sending if last time's answer was kept, since
        // a 304 has no body to fall back on.
        const held = meta.get(`index:${offset}`)
        const tag = held ? meta.get(`etag:${offset}`) : undefined
        const response = await get(`/posts?${query}`, {
          headers: tag ? { "If-None-Match": tag } : {},
        })

        let page: { total: number; items: Summary[] }
        if (response.status === 304) {
          page = JSON.parse(held!)
        } else {
          const body = await response.json()
          page = {
            total: body.total,
            items: body.items.map((item: Summary) => ({
              id: item.id,
              slug: item.slug,
              digest: item.digest,
              locale: item.locale,
            })),
          }
          meta.set(`etag:${offset}`, response.headers.get("etag") ?? "")
          meta.set(`index:${offset}`, JSON.stringify(page))
        }

        index.push(...page.items)
        if (index.length >= page.total || page.items.length === 0) break
      }

      // Only the posts whose digest moved are fetched in full. A build after a
      // change to one post is one request, not the archive.
      let fetched = 0
      for (const summary of index) {
        if (store.get(summary.id)?.digest === summary.digest) continue

        const post = await (await get(`/posts/${summary.id}`)).json()
        store.set({
          id: summary.id,
          data: await parseData({ id: summary.id, data: post }),
          rendered: { html: post.content_html },
          digest: summary.digest,
        })
        fetched += 1
      }

      const live = new Set(index.map((summary) => summary.id))
      for (const id of store.keys()) {
        if (!live.has(id)) store.delete(id)
      }

      logger.info(`${index.length} posts, ${fetched} changed`)
    },
  }
}
```

### 3. `src/content.config.ts`

```ts
import { defineCollection, z } from "astro:content"
import { posts } from "./loaders/mavicms"

const blog = defineCollection({
  loader: posts(),
  schema: z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    slug: z.string(),
    excerpt: z.string(),
    author: z.string(),
    category: z.string(),
    tags: z.array(z.string()),
    cover_url: z.string(),
    featured: z.boolean(),
    locale: z.string(),
    locales: z.array(z.string()),
    digest: z.string(),
    seo_title: z.string(),
    seo_description: z.string(),
    canonical: z.string(),
    created_at: z.coerce.date(),
    updated_at: z.coerce.date(),
  }),
})

export const collections = { blog }
```

### 4. `astro.config.mjs`

```js
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config"

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    // Astro 7.2. With a cacheKey on each page, a build regenerates the posts
    // that changed and copies the rest out of the cache.
    incrementalBuild: true,
  },
  // A site built from a CMS has no sessions of its own. Saying so keeps the
  // session runtime out of the bundle.
  session: false,
})
```

### 5. `src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro`

```astro
---
import { getCollection, render } from "astro:content"

export async function getStaticPaths() {
  const posts = await getCollection("blog")
  return posts.map((post) => ({
    params: { slug: post.data.slug },
    props: { post },
    // Astro 7.2. The page is rebuilt when this changes and taken from the
    // cache when it does not, which is the whole of what the digest is for.
    cacheKey: post.data.digest,
  }))
}

const { post } = Astro.props
const { Content } = await render(post)
---

<article>
  <h1>{post.data.title}</h1>
  <Content />
</article>
```

`astro dev` re-runs the loader on every reload, and after the first run almost
every one of those is a `304` and no work. `astro preview --background` (Astro
7.2) leaves a built site serving while you carry on, with
`astro preview status`, `logs` and `stop` to manage it.

### Sending a form from an Astro page

The submit address takes no token, so it can be called from the browser. What
it accepts is what the schema says, which means the form can be built from the
schema rather than written twice:

```ts
const schema = await fetch(`${API}/forms/contact/schema`).then((r) => r.json())

await fetch(`${API}/forms/contact/submit`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, message }),
})
```

## Publishing

`POST /publish` asks this site's build to run again — the same button the
panel has. Somebody writing a post presses it; a program rarely needs to.

## Rules of the road

- Ask for `status=published` unless you have a reason not to. Everything else
  is somebody's unfinished work.
- Page until you have `total`. The first fifty posts are not the archive.
- Key caches on `digest`, not on `updated_at`. A post saved with no changes
  keeps its digest, and rebuilding a site because somebody opened a post and
  closed it is the cost this field exists to avoid.
- Send `If-None-Match` back. It costs one header and saves the archive.
- The token reads. Anything that writes is a person signing in, and should be
  treated as one.
- Addresses beginning with `/` are relative to {{origin}}.
